name: Raven The
overview: The raven is depicted in Scripture as a black, solitary, and carnivorous bird, notable for being sent by Noah from the ark to explore the earth after the flood (Genesis 8:7). It is described as unclean and not to be eaten, emphasizing its distinct status among birds (Leviticus 11:15; Deuteronomy 14:14). Importantly, God used ravens to providentially feed the prophet Elijah during a time of drought, demonstrating divine care through these creatures (1 Kings 17:4-6). The raven’s plumage also serves as a symbol illustrating the glory of Christ, adding a Christ-centered dimension to its biblical portrayal.
